column2: req_desc

Run manifest
The app installs, builds and serves from `/app/run.json` on port 4173, and `GET /api/health` answers as qualified in Server boundary.

Grading seed and clock routes
`POST /api/grading/seed` creates a whole scenario in one call and `POST /api/grading/clock` sets and reads the server clock, both behind the grading token as published in API.

One error order and shape
Every API answers errors in the one published order, with the one published status per code and the one published body shape.

Roles and permissions
Each role can do only what the permission table allows, and a forbidden action answers with the published code and shows the published copy on screen.

Live updates without reload
Every change to the calendar, waiting room, ward board, Kennel beacon, consult note, stock, staff roles and online bookings reaches every other open window of the same clinic within the live-update limit, with no reload.

Published animations and reduced motion
Every published animation exposes its `data-motion`, `data-motion-ms` and `data-motion-easing`, and under reduced motion each reads `none` and `0` with the final state shown at once.

Responsive layouts at three viewports
Every screen shows its published layout at 375x812, 768x1024 and 1280x800 with no horizontal overflow and tap targets of at least 44 px.

Published names and live regions
Every control and region in the public table is reachable by its exact role and accessible name, and the `Announcements` region and the `alert` regions carry the published copy.

Look: palette, type and shapes
The product uses the published palette roles, the two named typefaces, the flat tinted-card language, the corner shapes and the very large Kennel beacon numerals, with WCAG 2.2 AA contrast.

Composition, split band and public page
The clinic header, screen split band, pill buttons, patient cards, history layout, invoice footnote block, empty and outage cards, workspace footer, and the public page's hero, chooser cards, services tiles and meet the vets band look as described in Screens and layout and Visual design.

Server clock decides time in source
No browser code decides due, overdue, late, waiting minutes, booking windows, batch expiry, reminder sending, undo lifetime or the clinic date from the browser's own clock or zone.

Configuration from env
Every service URL, credential and setting is read from the environment at start and is never hard-coded or sent to the browser.

Day calendar structure, slot names and clinic date
The `Day calendar` grid shows one column per consult room and one gridcell per slot with its published name, each appointment is a button with its published name, and the calendar opens on the clinic's own date with every time in clinic time whatever zone or clock the browser has.

Keyboard booking and the error summary
The calendar and `Book appointment` are fully operable by keyboard with focus kept inside and returned on close, and an incomplete or rejected booking shows the in-dialog error summary as published in Feedback states.

One winner per slot
Simultaneous claims of the same vet or room slot have exactly one winner by server order, and the loser gets the slot-taken code and copy.

Keyboard booking journey
A coordinator books by keyboard, meets the error summary, loses the race to a second window and sees the conflict, the live `booked` state and the focus return.

Move, resize, cancel and undo rules
Appointments move, resize, cancel and restore through the published endpoints under the published state rules, and a restore works only within `UNDO_SECONDS` of the server clock.

Keyboard move, resize, cancel and undo
The published key commands move, resize, check in, cancel and undo a focused appointment with focus staying on the moved block, and only one undo toast exists, retargeted by the newest cancel.

Move and undo journey
A coordinator moves, lengthens, cancels twice and restores by keyboard while a second window follows each step without reload.

Phone and tablet calendar layouts and closed menu
At 768 px only the `Day calendar` grid exists with the published panel order, at 375 px only the `Day agenda` exists, and a closed `Menu` drawer or closed `Manage` panel is absent from the accessibility tree and the Tab order.

Long-press drag on touch
On a touch viewport a 500 ms long-press picks an appointment up, dragging moves it and releasing drops it on the slot under the finger.

Phone and tablet calendar journey
A coordinator moves an appointment by long-press and drag on a tablet while a desktop window shows the move, the phone shows the agenda, and reduced motion removes every animation.

Appointment lifecycle and check-in rules
Appointments move through booked, checked-in, in-consult, completed, cancelled and no-show only along the published edges, and every other edge is rejected with the published code.

Waiting room list, minutes and honest start
The `Waiting room` list orders checked-in patients by check-in time, shows server-computed waiting minutes that advance on the published tick, shows the published empty state, and removes a row on `Start consult for <Patient>` only on the server's answer or the live push.

Late arrivals written as text
A booked appointment becomes late by the server clock after the published late minutes, and lateness and late arrivals are written as text chips and in names with AA contrast, never as colour alone.

Check-in journey
A coordinator checks a late patient in, the vet's window shows the arrival and the minutes advance, two vets start the same consult, and the row leaves both windows with one winner.

Consult note paragraphs and versions
A consult note is a list of versioned paragraphs where the first save of a version wins, a stale save is rejected with the published code, and edits to different paragraphs both apply.

Live co-editing, saves and draft box
Two vets see each other's paragraph text live, a window never conflicts with itself or loses text typed during a save, a stale save shows the published message with the loser's text in a `Draft` box, and both windows converge, also after reload.

Co-edit journey
Two vets type in different paragraphs, then collide on one paragraph, and both end on the same text after reload.

Treatment schedules and due, overdue rules
Treatment doses are scheduled in elapsed hours from a first dose typed in clinic time, with the published rules for times that do not exist or occur twice, and each dose is upcoming, due or overdue by the server clock and the published grace.

Ward board names and Kennel beacon digits
The `Ward board` shows each treatment as a cell with its published name and group, and the three Kennel beacon cards carry server counts in `data-value` built from per-digit elements that roll only when changed.

Marking given, reopening and skipping
Marking a treatment given, reopening or skipping it follows the published rules, and each server result or rejection is announced with the patient and treatment name.

Ward journey
The clock advances so a cell turns `Due` then `Overdue`, the `Overdue` tally rolls its changed digits, a nurse marks the cell given and the second nurse's board matches.

Ward board keyboard
Arrow keys, Space, Shift+Space, N and S operate the ward board by the published movement rules, and Escape closes any ward dialog and returns focus to its cell.

Ward dialogs and refreshes keep UI state
`Skip treatment` and `Add note` validate in place with an error summary, and an open dialog, its summary, its text, the focus and any shown message survive every timed or pushed refresh.

Ward timers journey
A nurse opens a note, types, lets the clock cross due and overdue, finishes the note, and reopens a given cell by keyboard, also under reduced motion.

Invoice money in integer pence
Invoice lines, discounts, VAT and totals are integer pence with the published per-line half-up rounding, and the invoice screen, footnotes and PDF show the same amounts.

Invoice lifecycle, payments and replayed keys
Invoices move through draft, issued, part-paid, paid and voided only along the published edges, a payment above the balance is rejected, and a replayed `Idempotency-Key` returns the stored result.

Invoice screen by keyboard and lost responses
The invoice screen adds stock lines, applies a discount, issues and takes payment entirely by keyboard, validates the payment amount in place, and sends one key per attempt so a lost response never pays or draws twice.

Attributed void
Voiding an invoice needs a reason, and the void, its stock returns and every payment record who did it and when, on screen and in the invoice PDF.

Invoice journey
A vet builds and issues an invoice by keyboard, a coordinator takes a part payment through a lost response and an overpayment attempt, and an unpaid invoice is voided with a reason, ending on the published balances, statuses and attribution.

Stock ledger, batches and first-expiry-first-out
Stock is held in batches with expiry dates, each invoice line draws from usable batches first-expiry-first-out exactly once, removal or void returns each draw to its own batch through a paired movement, every movement carries its running balance, and concurrent claims on the last usable units have exactly as many winners as units.

Low-stock alert, expiry edge and live count
When usable stock drops to or below an item's reorder point by a movement or by a batch expiring at clinic midnight, `Low stock` and exactly one announcement appear live in every manager window, and the low-stock count always equals the server's.

Stock journey
A line drawn across two batches drops stock once per batch, the manager sees the live low-stock badge, a void returns each draw, the movement list's running balances end on on-hand, and a batch expiring at clinic midnight changes usable stock and alerts once.

Online booking window, confirmation and rate limit
Online booking offers only free slots from the lead time to the horizon in clinic time, rejects any other start with the published code, shows a confirmation readable only by its unguessable code, and answers as published once the attempt limit is reached.

Owner text in email
The owner's typed names are accepted only as 1 to 80 characters without control characters, the pet name reaches the confirmation email subject and the owner name the first line of its body exactly with non-ASCII text intact, and a name carrying a line break is refused and sends nothing.

Public booking page on a phone
At 375 px the public booking page is touch-operable in the published order, always shows times for the latest chosen day and reason, keeps the chosen time and typed details across the 15-second refresh, and creates one booking per confirm.

Online booking journey
A pet owner on a phone books by touch with a non-London browser zone and sees the exact confirmation and email, and the staff calendar shows the new block live.

Reminder schedule
A vaccination reminder is sent at the published hour of clinic time on the calendar day the published number of days before the due date, once per vaccine per due date, with the published rules for jumped, late-recorded and missed reminders.

Reminder email and Sent status
The reminder email has the published subject and link, and the patient's reminder reads `Sent` only after SMTP accepts it.

Reminder link scope
A reminder's pet token pre-fills the booking page only under its own clinic and only until the end of the vaccine's due date in clinic time, and otherwise answers 404 and shows the plain booking page.

Reminder journey
Advancing the clock to the send moment delivers exactly one reminder, the patient shows `Sent`, a second advance sends no duplicate, and the link opens the booking page for that pet.

File upload and listing
Uploads go through the app to MinIO byte for byte with their submitted name and checksum, never overwrite a same-named file, and are listed on `Files` with a preview only after the put is confirmed.

Safe file serving
File type is judged only by the full signature at byte 0, and every stored file is served with its sniffed type, the no-sniff header and the sandbox policy so an HTML file named as an X-ray can never be stored or run.

Storage outage
With storage down the health route reports `unavailable`, uploads and exports fail with the published copy, and nothing half-made is listed or stored.

PDF exports
The history and invoice PDFs are produced in the app with the published text layer, one page per 25 lines, attachments only with `?include=files`, and the bytes returned equal the exported object.

Files journey
A manager uploads an X-ray and sees it listed and announced, the outage instance shows the exact alert with nothing listed, and the history PDF lists the file only when asked.

Staff invitations, sign-in and landing
The manager invites staff through Mailpit, the invitee sets a password and lands on `Today`, and sign-in lands on a safe same-origin `next` path or on `Today` and sign-out on the sign-in page, as published.

Role change and removal
The manager changes a staff member's role or removes their access, and that person's very next request and open windows obey the new role or end the session within two seconds, while a manager cannot change or remove their own access.

Clinic tenancy
A clinic's records, files, PDFs, staff and search results are reachable only inside that clinic, and another clinic's id answers as a missing record.

Invite and tenancy journey
The manager invites a nurse who signs in through a record link and lands on it, sees the forbidden copy on invoices, gets a missing-record answer for another clinic's id, and the manager's invoice PDF text layer and page count are exact.
`/app/run.json` has string `install`, `build` and `serve` and `"_schema":"run-manifest-v1"`, and `serve` starts the app on port 4173 on `0.0.0.0`.

A `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` at the project root lists every shipped package (the production dependency tree from `npm ls --omit=dev --all --json`), plus the two fonts, each with name, version and licence.
Every shipped package (the production dependency tree) and font has an open licence (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC or SIL Open Font License); none is copyleft or proprietary.
The app uses no datastore beyond Postgres, Mailpit and MinIO: no Redis, SQLite, local file storage for patient files, or in-memory state that survives only a process.
The provided service definitions and their dev credentials are left untouched.
The package lockfile is committed and fonts and images are bundled; nothing loads from another origin at runtime.
